aweme_info.desc: Ten months ago, I was a very different woman. I weighed 96kg, was struggling with my mental health and had spent almost two years isolating myself from the world, barely living and fighting battles in my own mind that very few people knew about. Living with bipolar disorder and EUPD, carrying the trauma of childhood sexual assault and battling periods of suicidal ideation, there were times I genuinely couldn’t see the life I have today. But somewhere along the way, I made a decision. I wanted more for myself. I wanted to live, not just survive. I started changing my life, one decision at a time. I changed my habits, walked away from things that were holding me back and started showing up for myself. No weight loss injections. No shortcuts. Just hard work, consistency, discipline and a determination to rebuild myself. Ten months later, I’m 68.8kg, 27.2kg down, stronger than I’ve ever been, running, lifting weights, challenging myself and doing things I once never imagined possible. But the biggest transformation isn’t on the scales. It’s the confidence I’ve found, the friendships I’ve made, the smile I wear and the life I’m finally living. My past will always be part of my story, but it will never get to write the rest of it. To anyone silently fighting battles behind closed doors, please believe that your story isn’t over. You deserve to experience happiness, love, purpose and a life beyond simply surviving. At 42, I’m not chasing perfection. I’m building a life I’m proud of. I spent years losing myself. These last 10 months have been about finding myself again. And this time, I’m choosing ME. Every single day. ❤️ #bpd #bipolar #MentalHealthMatters #HealingJourney #fyp

original_client_text.markup_text:
Ten months ago, I was a very different woman. I weighed 96kg, was struggling with my mental health and had spent almost two years isolating myself from the world, barely living and fighting battles in my own mind that very few people knew about.

Living with bipolar disorder and EUPD, carrying the trauma of childhood sexual assault and battling periods of suicidal ideation, there were times I genuinely couldn’t see the life I have today.

But somewhere along the way, I made a decision. I wanted more for myself. I wanted to live, not just survive.

I started changing my life, one decision at a time. I changed my habits, walked away from things that were holding me back and started showing up for myself.

No weight loss injections. No shortcuts. Just hard work, consistency, discipline and a determination to rebuild myself.

Ten months later, I’m 68.8kg, 27.2kg down, stronger than I’ve ever been, running, lifting weights, challenging myself and doing things I once never imagined possible.

But the biggest transformation isn’t on the scales. It’s the confidence I’ve found, the friendships I’ve made, the smile I wear and the life I’m finally living.

My past will always be part of my story, but it will never get to write the rest of it.

To anyone silently fighting battles behind closed doors, please believe that your story isn’t over. You deserve to experience happiness, love, purpose and a life beyond simply surviving.

At 42, I’m not chasing perfection. I’m building a life I’m proud of.

I spent years losing myself. These last 10 months have been about finding myself again.

And this time, I’m choosing ME. Every single day. ❤️

#bpd #bipolar #MentalHealthMatters #HealingJourney #fyp

aweme_info.desc: I’ve gained weight since the end of this video. About 35 pounds over the last 14 months. And I still stand behind every single thing this transformation taught me and the tools that helped me lose 200+ pounds naturally. I think there’s something we get wrong about “sustainable” weight loss. It doesn’t mean your weight never fluctuates again. That life never gets hard. That you never go through a season where you move less, eat differently, travel more, recover from surgery, fall in love, experience grief or simply have less capacity to prioritize your health. That’s real life. These last 6 months have included a major surgery and recovery, so much travel and living out of hotels, falling in love and experiencing some “happy weight” 🫣 and one of the hardest months of my life sitting beside my brother in the hospital. And I gained weight. But I didn’t lose what I learned. Years ago, regaining weight would’ve made me feel like I failed. I would’ve thought I ruined everything and needed some extreme new plan to “get back on track.” Or I would’ve given up altogether. But today, I know what to do because I spent years learning how to actually care for myself by shifting my mindset, changing my habits, learning new rhythms and understanding my emotional journey. And those are the exact tools I put into my Getting Started Guide. They’re the tools I’m going back to right now, not to punish myself for gaining weight (I actually have a lot of grace for myself in this season), but because I’m ready to give my health more of my attention again. That may be one of the greatest things this journey has given me. I don’t have to be afraid of gaining weight because I trust myself to know how to move forward. Because I know I’m changed. Sustainable health isn’t about never needing to find your way back. It’s about being confident that you know how to. ❤️ *link to guide in bio

original_client_text.markup_text:
I’ve gained weight since the end of this video. About 35 pounds over the last 14 months. And I still stand behind every single thing this transformation taught me and the tools that helped me lose 200+ pounds naturally.

I think there’s something we get wrong about “sustainable” weight loss. It doesn’t mean your weight never fluctuates again. That life never gets hard. That you never go through a season where you move less, eat differently, travel more, recover from surgery, fall in love, experience grief or simply have less capacity to prioritize your health. That’s real life.

These last 6 months have included a major surgery and recovery, so much travel and living out of hotels, falling in love and experiencing some “happy weight” 🫣 and one of the hardest months of my life sitting beside my brother in the hospital.

And I gained weight. But I didn’t lose what I learned.

Years ago, regaining weight would’ve made me feel like I failed. I would’ve thought I ruined everything and needed some extreme new plan to “get back on track.” Or I would’ve given up altogether.

But today, I know what to do because I spent years learning how to actually care for myself by shifting my mindset, changing my habits, learning new rhythms and understanding my emotional journey.

And those are the exact tools I put into my Getting Started Guide. They’re the tools I’m going back to right now, not to punish myself for gaining weight (I actually have a lot of grace for myself in this season), but because I’m ready to give my health more of my attention again.

That may be one of the greatest things this journey has given me. I don’t have to be afraid of gaining weight because I trust myself to know how to move forward. Because I know I’m changed.

Sustainable health isn’t about never needing to find your way back. It’s about being confident that you know how to. ❤️

*link to guide in bio

original_client_text.markup_text:
Day 12 of my weight loss journey! 🥹💪🔥

📅 October 11: 235.4 lbs
⚖️ October 22: 233 lbs
🎯 Goal: 150 lbs — 85 pounds to lose!

I’m recording these videos shirtless because I want to SEE my body change over time. No hiding, no filters, just real progress. 📸

I’m not happy with where I’m at physically, but I know I can change that. This is only the beginning. 💯

❤️ Follow me if you want to watch me lose 85 pounds and transform my life!

I also hope these videos inspire someone else to pick up their phone and document their own weight loss journey. You don’t have to wait until you look different to start. 🫶

💬 Anyone else starting their weight loss journey? What’s your goal weight? 👇

#WeightLossJourney #WeightLossTransformation #WeightLossMotivation #FitnessJourney #FYP

aweme_info.desc: MY WEIGHT-LOSS JOURNEY ❤️ I’ve thought about sharing this for a while, and today I finally decided to tell my story. I started this journey weighing 105kg, and today I’m around 68kg. That’s almost 37kg gone. 🥹❤️ But let me tell you something… it wasn’t easy. There were days I felt tired. There were days I wanted to give up. There were days I looked in the mirror and didn’t even recognize the person I was becoming. But I kept reminding myself that I started this journey for ME. I learned that weight loss is not about starving yourself or trying to become someone else. It’s about making better choices, being consistent, moving your body, being patient with yourself, and understanding that progress takes time. And most importantly, I learned that your health matters more than a number on the scale. If you’re currently on your own weight-loss journey, please don’t compare your progress to someone else’s. Your body is YOUR body. Take it one day at a time. Celebrate the small wins. Be patient with yourself. ❤️ And please, don’t be afraid of food. Learn to nourish your body, not punish it. Eat well, rest, and listen to your body. To the person who is just starting: you can do this. 🥹❤️ You don’t need to lose 30kg tomorrow. You just need to keep showing up for yourself. One day, you’ll look back and realize how far you’ve come. This journey changed my body, but more importantly, it changed my mindset. If I can start, stay consistent, and keep going, so can you. ❤️ Here’s to becoming healthier, happier, stronger and more confident—not perfect. 🥂❤️ #MyWeightLossJourney #WeightLossJourney #HealthyLifestyle #Consistency #SelfLove

original_client_text.markup_text:
MY WEIGHT-LOSS JOURNEY ❤️

I’ve thought about sharing this for a while, and today I finally decided to tell my story.

I started this journey weighing 105kg, and today I’m around 68kg. That’s almost 37kg gone. 🥹❤️

But let me tell you something… it wasn’t easy.

There were days I felt tired. There were days I wanted to give up. There were days I looked in the mirror and didn’t even recognize the person I was becoming. But I kept reminding myself that I started this journey for ME.

I learned that weight loss is not about starving yourself or trying to become someone else. It’s about making better choices, being consistent, moving your body, being patient with yourself, and understanding that progress takes time.

And most importantly, I learned that your health matters more than a number on the scale.

If you’re currently on your own weight-loss journey, please don’t compare your progress to someone else’s. Your body is YOUR body. Take it one day at a time. Celebrate the small wins. Be patient with yourself. ❤️

And please, don’t be afraid of food. Learn to nourish your body, not punish it. Eat well, rest, and listen to your body.

To the person who is just starting: you can do this. 🥹❤️

You don’t need to lose 30kg tomorrow. You just need to keep showing up for yourself.

One day, you’ll look back and realize how far you’ve come.

This journey changed my body, but more importantly, it changed my mindset.

If I can start, stay consistent, and keep going, so can you. ❤️

Here’s to becoming healthier, happier, stronger and more confident—not perfect. 🥂❤️

#MyWeightLossJourney #WeightLossJourney #HealthyLifestyle #Consistency #SelfLove

original_client_text.markup_text:
Ep. 05 | Duppy, Gunman or Diabetes? 👻💙

At 16, I lost 51 pounds in less than three months. And while everybody was busy diagnosing me with everything from obeah to AIDS, the real culprit nearly k*lled me.

November is Diabetes Awareness Month, and if my story teaches you anything, let it be this: Know the 4 Ts of Diabetes.

💧 Thirst – Excessive thirst
🚽 Toilet – Frequent urination
😴 Tired – Unusual fatigue
⚖️ Thinner – Unexplained weight loss

These can be warning signs of diabetes. Please seek medical attention early. Don’t wait until it’s an emergency.

Big up Spanish Town Hospital. You saved my life. 💙

P.S. I’m not a doctor. This is my experience, not medical advice. Gwaan a doctor if you feel sick, TikTok is no hospital.

#DiabetesAwarenessMonth #DiabetesAwareness #DiabetesSymptoms #EarlyActionOnDiabetes #jamaicatiktok

aweme_info.desc: To our brothers and sisters in the Rohingya community, Today, I am sharing a story that deeply impacted me, one that serves as an urgent reminder of our shared duty to one another. I recently reconnected with Mohammad Islam, a member of our Rohingya community who arrived in the United States twelve years ago. After enduring two painful years in jail, he returned to a life of homelessness. During his hardest moments, he was left without support, care, or a community to lean on. When I saw him today at Walmart, I was able to help him with essential clothing, a phone, and financial assistance to secure shelter. While I am grateful I was in a position to step in, no one in our community should ever have to suffer through hardship alone. As Rohingya people, we know the weight of struggle, displacement, and loss. That history makes it even more crucial that we stand strong, remain united, and protect our own. Our unity is our greatest strength, and helping those among us who have fallen on hard times is not just an act of kindness it is our collective responsibility and our right. Let this be a call to action for all of us:  Stay United: Leave no one behind, regardless of their past or current circumstances.  Look Out for One Another: Check in on community members who are struggling, isolated, or in need of support.  Act with Compassion: Lend a helping hand whether through financial aid, shelter, food, or simply human connection. We have overcome immense challenges together, and we must continue to uplift each other here and now. Let us commit to building a stronger, more compassionate Rohingya community where every individual is cared for and valued. In unity and solidarity, Sadek Khan Community Activist #sadekkhanofficial #rohingya #humanity

original_client_text.markup_text:
To our brothers and sisters in the Rohingya community,
Today, I am sharing a story that deeply impacted me, one that serves as an urgent reminder of our shared duty to one another.
I recently reconnected with Mohammad Islam, a member of our Rohingya community who arrived in the United States twelve years ago. After enduring two painful years in jail, he returned to a life of homelessness. During his hardest moments, he was left without support, care, or a community to lean on. When I saw him today at Walmart, I was able to help him with essential clothing, a phone, and financial assistance to secure shelter.
While I am grateful I was in a position to step in, no one in our community should ever have to suffer through hardship alone.
As Rohingya people, we know the weight of struggle, displacement, and loss. That history makes it even more crucial that we stand strong, remain united, and protect our own. Our unity is our greatest strength, and helping those among us who have fallen on hard times is not just an act of kindness it is our collective responsibility and our right.
Let this be a call to action for all of us:
Stay United: Leave no one behind, regardless of their past or current circumstances.
Look Out for One Another: Check in on community members who are struggling, isolated, or in need of support.
Act with Compassion: Lend a helping hand whether through financial aid, shelter, food, or simply human connection.
We have overcome immense challenges together, and we must continue to uplift each other here and now. Let us commit to building a stronger, more compassionate Rohingya community where every individual is cared for and valued.
In unity and solidarity,
Sadek Khan
Community Activist #sadekkhanofficial #rohingya #humanity
